column1: Do Organisms create exact copies of themselves?

column2: Chromosomes in the nucleus contain information for inheritance.
DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid) carries hereditary information.
DNA in nucleus acts as information source for making proteins.
If information changes, different proteins are formed.
Basic event in reproduction is creation of DNA copies.
Cells use chemical reactions to build copies of DNA.
Two copies of DNA are produced during reproduction.
DNA copying is accompanied by creation of cellular structures.
Process of copying DNA introduces variations.
DNA copies generated are similar but not identical.
Some variations may not survive in environment.
Surviving cells are similar but slightly different.
The Importance of Variation

column3: Consistency of DNA copying helps maintain body design.
Variations allow organisms to occupy different niches.
If population faces adverse conditions, some variations help survival.
Variations are useful for survival of species over time.

column1: Modes of Reproduction Used by Single Organisms

column2: Fission

column3: Occurs mainly in unicellular organisms.
Many bacteria and protozoans divide into two equal halves.
Amoeba splits into two cells during division.
Leishmania divides in a definite orientation.
Plasmodium divides into many daughter cells simultaneously.
Yeast can put out small buds which later separate.

column2: Fragmentation

column3: Multicellular organisms cannot simply divide cells.
Body organization is more complex.
Organisms break into fragments and each grows separately.
Carefully organized cell division is required.

column2: Regeneration

column3: Some organisms can regenerate lost body parts.
Cut or broken pieces grow into complete individuals.
Hydra and Planaria show regeneration.
Specialized cells divide rapidly during regeneration.
New cells form different tissues and organs.

column2: Budding

column3: Hydra reproduces by budding.
Bud develops as an outgrowth due to repeated cell division.
Bud grows into a tiny individual.
Later it detaches and becomes independent.

column2: Vegetative Propagation

column3: New plants can grow from roots, stems or leaves.
Common methods include layering and grafting.
Used widely in agriculture.
Plants produced are genetically similar to parent plant.
Bryophyllum develops buds on leaf margins.
These buds grow into new plants under suitable conditions.

column2: Spore Formation

column3: Thread-like structures develop on bread mould.
These structures bear spores.
Spores are covered by thick walls.
They survive under unfavorable conditions.
Under suitable conditions spores germinate into new organisms.

column2: Creation of two individuals from different parents occurs.
Every individual is genetically unique.
Sexual reproduction introduces more variation.
DNA copying mechanism is not perfect.
Variations accumulate over generations.
Some variations are beneficial for survival.
Genetic material from two parents combines.
One copy of genetic material comes from each parent.
Sexual reproduction requires formation of gametes.
Stamen and pistil are reproductive parts of flower.
Stamen is male reproductive organ.

column3: It produces pollen grains.

column2: Pistil is female reproductive organ.

column3: It consists of stigma, style and ovary.

column2: Pollen grains contain male gametes.
Ovules contain female gametes.
Transfer of pollen from anther to stigma is pollination.
Self-pollination occurs within same flower.
Cross-pollination occurs between different flowers.
After pollination pollen tube grows towards ovule.
Fertilization occurs when male gamete fuses with female gamete.
Ovule develops into seed.
Ovary develops into fruit.
Seed germinates into new plant under suitable conditions.
Male Reproductive System

column3: Testes produce male gametes called sperms.
Testes are located outside abdominal cavity.
Testosterone brings changes during puberty.
Sperm formation begins at puberty.
Sperms are delivered through vas deferens.
Secretions from glands provide nutrition to sperms.
Female Reproductive System
Ovaries produce female gametes called ova.
One ovum matures periodically.
Oviducts carry ovum towards uterus.
Uterus is a muscular organ.
Fertilization may occur in oviduct.
Embryo implants in uterus wall.
Placenta provides nutrition to embryo.

column2: Menstruation

column3: If egg is not fertilized, uterine lining breaks down.
Blood and tissues are discharged through vagina.
This process is called menstruation.
Menstrual cycle usually lasts 28 days.

column2: Reproductive health means healthy reproductive system.
Sexually transmitted diseases can spread through unsafe practices.
Contraceptive methods help avoid unwanted pregnancy.
Barrier methods prevent sperm from reaching egg.
Condoms help prevent infections.
Surgical methods are also used for contraception.
